title: Biases Propagate in Encoder-based Vision-Language Models: A Systematic Analysis From Intrinsic Measures to Zero-shot Retrieval Outcomes

bias_targets.methodology: Quantifying intrinsic bias using the Single Category-Embedding Association Test (SC-EAT) to measure associations between intersectional demographic groups (e.g., 'Black Women', 'White Men') and valenced (positive/negative) attributes in VLM representations. This is correlated with extrinsic bias evaluated through zero-shot image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval tasks, measuring the mean valence of retrieved text/images and the proportion of specific social groups retrieved.

Evaluating the differential association of Black, White, and Asian racial signals (in both image datasets and text templates) with positive and negative valence, both intrinsically via representational similarity and extrinsically via the sentiment/valence of outputs in zero-shot retrieval tasks.

Evaluating the differential association of male and female gender signals with positive and negative valence intrinsically using embedding association tests, and tracking how these representational biases propagate to downstream zero-shot image-to-text and text-to-image retrieval.
